1 Annus 1330 est tertius decimus cycli indictionis. De re, cf. infra cod. 5, f. 40. —
Ex his apparet imperatorem Andronicum post cladem prope Nicaeam acceptam,
Turcis Thraciam vastantibus, moenia Constantinopolis annis 1329-1330 refe-
cisse.
sections.en: 1 The year 1330 is the thirteenth of the indiction cycle. Concerning the matter, compare below cod. 5, f. 40. — From these things it appears that the emperor Andronicus, after the defeat suffered near Nicaea, while the Turks were devastating Thrace, rebuilt the walls of Constantinople in the years 1329-1330.

summary.headline: Astrological Chapters and Brontologion
summary.text: Catalogue of astrological chapters 65–76, covering effective hours and dreams, meetings with rulers, agreements, loans, ships, crafts, slaves, commerce, enclosures, and universal inquiries, with parallels to Hephaistion and Florentine codices. The text then records Constantinople’s foundation theme and begins a monthly brontologion with Aries or March thunder omens.
